description: Apply EDL's render rule, judged by both sides on the same canvases (decided 2026-10-04: the badge is split by surface, and whatever is anchored at a render judges with the render's own rule). Each case is a canvas: the Apply EDL node is `render`, with the producers wired into it holding their saved results. `sources` is what its Sources wires deliver, in slot order; a render lists its own `sources` when a list wired into Sources fans the render out. `renders` lists the renders a run of `render` makes, in order (a list that fans the render out renders once per row, `clip` naming the row: a plan's clip, a List's row): the EDL each one reads, and what the server says about it — its issues, or none when it renders. The server test (apply-edl-render-rule-parity.test.ts, beside this folder) runs the canvas the way a Run from here at the render does (saved results seeded, the fan-out, the input resolver, the DAG payload builder); the route test (backend/src/routes/__tests__/apply-edl-render-rule-parity.test.ts) sends each render to POST /v1/apply-edl, as a single-node Run does; the editor test (frontend/src/lib/__tests__/apply-edl-render-rule-parity.test.ts) runs the editor's own Run of `render` (the fan-out planned, each render's inputs resolved), then takes the renders the panel badge judges and runs its render verdict. All three must reach these verdicts. Where a run makes several renders, the badge judges each with its own EDL and Sources and names each issue by its render, numbered from 1 by its row (`render 2: …`); `badgeIssues` is set only where the editor words the same refusal differently: on a case, the badge's whole list; on one render of several, that render's issues as the badge names them.

ready.note: A single-camera Tighten plan the renderer draws as it is: one render, nothing refused.

layouts.note: Camera Switch with layout hints on: a side-by-side, two-slot layout is a well-formed EDL that this renderer cannot draw (one source full frame per segment).

issues: segment[1] "s1": layout mode "side-by-side" — this renderer shows one source full-frame per segment (multi-camera layouts are a speaker-view feature)
segment[1] "s1": layout with 2 slots — this renderer shows one source per segment (multi-slot layouts are a speaker-view feature)

over the 180-minute cap.note: A Text node holding one EDL (a wire that is not a plan delivers ONE value per run) that renders 181 minutes: over the cap for one render.

issues: the edit renders 181 minutes of output — over the 180-minute limit for one render; split it into parts of at most 180 minutes

a default crossfade brings it under the.note: An inline EDL 2 s over 180 minutes; the node's Default crossfade of 1 s at its two boundaries overlaps 2 s, so the output is exactly 180 minutes.

the same edit with hard cuts.note: The edit above with Default crossfade 0: 180.1 minutes, over the cap.

issues: the edit renders 180.1 minutes of output — over the 180-minute limit for one render; split it into parts of at most 180 minutes

an unknown role.note: A misspelled master-audio role: only a warning in the EDL contract, refused by the renderer (it would take each segment's sound from its own camera).

issues: source "mic": unknown role "master_audio" — this renderer knows only master-audio, camera, wide, screen (a misspelled "master-audio" would take each segment's sound from its own camera)

a segment with no picture, video output.note: A segment with sound (master audio) but no picture source: a video render needs a picture on every segment.

issues: segment[1] "s1" has no video source (required for a video-output edit; use output:"audio" for an audio-only cut)

a segment with no picture, audio output.note: The same plan rendered as audio: the picture is never read.

a read before a source starts, video out.note: cam2 starts 3 s into the master clock (offsetMs 3000); the segment reads its picture from 1 s.

issues: segment[0] "s0": starts at 1000ms on the master clock but source "cam2" begins at 3000ms (offsetMs) — the segment would read before the source starts

a read before a source starts, audio out.note: The same plan rendered as audio reads only the master audio, which starts at 0.

an inline list.note: A list typed into the node's own EDL renders whole, as one EDL, which it is not. The server reads it as an EDL with no segments; the editor names the list.

issues: segments is empty

badgeIssues: expected one EDL, got a list

a chapters plan.note: An Edit Plan in chapters mode wired into the render: a wired value that is not an EDL is an invalid EDL, not 'no EDL'.

issues: segments is empty

an Edit Plan clip list.note: Clips mode: one render per clip. The second clip carries a region crop, which this renderer cannot draw.

issues: segment[0] "c1s0": region crops are not renderable here (a speaker-view feature) — remove segment.region

a Camera Switch batch held as JSON strin.note: Camera Switch run once per clip holds its latest batch on __listResults, one JSON STRING per clip, with '' for a clip whose run failed (skipped, as the fan-out skips it). The third clip switches with an xfade, which this renderer cannot draw.

issues: segment[1] "seg-1": layout transition "xfade:fade" is not renderable here (only "cut", or a segment `transition` of type "crossfade", is) — remove it or use segment.transition

an empty url a wired source fills.note: The plan's source has no url; the media wired into the render's Sources input fills it, positionally. Structurally the plan has an empty url; as a render it is complete.

a source wire that delivers nothing.note: Two Sources wires: the first comes from an upload with no media yet, which delivers nothing, so the second wire's media takes slot 0 and fills source 'a'.

the last wire holding an EDL.note: Two plans wired into EDL; the later wire's plan has not run, so it delivers nothing and the earlier wire's plan renders.

issues: the edit renders 181 minutes of output — over the 180-minute limit for one render; split it into parts of at most 180 minutes

a List of EDLs.note: A List holding one EDL per row fans the render out, one render per row, like a plan's clip list: the second row's side-by-side layout is refused for that render alone.

issues: segment[1] "s1": layout mode "side-by-side" — this renderer shows one source full-frame per segment (multi-camera layouts are a speaker-view feature)
segment[1] "s1": layout with 2 slots — this renderer shows one source per segment (multi-slot layouts are a speaker-view feature)

Generate Text items, one EDL per item.note: Generate Text wired from its Items output delivers one item per run (its text split on ===NEXT===), so each item is its own render; its whole text is not one EDL.

Camera Switch's transcript wired into th.note: This wire leaves Camera Switch's Transcript output, not its switched EDL: the render reads the transcript as its EDL, which has no segments.

issues: segments is empty

a List wired into Sources, a row missing.note: Two columns of a List wired into Sources fan the render out, one render per row, each row's media filling the plan's sources in slot order. The second row has no second camera: its render gets one override, so the plan's second source keeps its empty url and that render alone is refused.

issues: source "cam2": url is empty (media resolves from url)
source "cam2" has no url — resolve it or wire a `sources` override

a clip list paired with a List of source.note: A plan's clip list and a List wired into Sources with the same rows fan the render out together: each render reads its clip and its row's media, in slot order. The second clip cuts between two cameras but its row brings one, so its second source keeps its empty url and that render alone is refused; the first renders.

issues: source "cam2": url is empty (media resolves from url)
source "cam2" has no url — resolve it or wire a `sources` override

a List row with no EDL that its camera k.note: A List's EDL column is wired into EDL and its camera column into Sources. The second row's EDL cell is empty, but its camera cell keeps the row in the run, so the run still makes that render with no EDL: the server refuses it (an empty EDL has no segments) and the editor's Run refuses it before sending ("apply-edl requires an EDL"). The badge counts it as a render that fails with no EDL, so the node is not ready.

issues: segments is empty
